title: After 28 Years on Foot, Karl Bushby Finally Walks Home
summary:
Twenty-eight years. That is how long it took Karl Bushby to walk home.

Bushby, a British adventurer, has become the first person to travel all the way around the world on foot or by swimming. He set off from Punta Arenas in Chile on 1 November 1998, when he was 29 years old. He expected the trip of about 31,000 miles to take around 12 years. On 2 November 2026, he finally reached his mother's home in Hull, England.

The idea began with a birthday card from his father, mentioning a debate about whether someone could walk from London to New York through the Bering Strait. Bushby traced a route to Alaska, then stretched it to the southern tip of South America.

He set himself two rules: he would move forward only by walking or swimming, and he would not return to the United Kingdom until he had finished the whole journey on foot.

He began with a basic survival kit, a cart for his supplies and about 500 dollars, and no sponsors. Strangers often shared food and shelter. His father Keith said Bushby once walked for three days over the Andes on just one banana.

In 2006, he and French-American adventurer Dimitri Kieffer crossed the icy Bering Strait between Alaska and Russia, following a winding route of about 150 miles in temperatures as low as minus 31 degrees Fahrenheit. After 15 hard days they reached Russia.

By late September 2026 he had reached France. After getting permission from French and British authorities, Bushby swam the Channel for about 20 hours over three days, reaching Dover on 5 October. Then he walked about 250 more miles to Hull, where his mother Angela was waiting. She greeted him with a simple question: 'Where have you been?'
why_it_matters: Bushby's journey shows what stubborn determination can achieve over a lifetime, and it reminds us that huge goals can be reached one small step at a time.

keywords.explanation: An adventurer is someone who takes on bold and risky journeys.
The Bering Strait is the narrow sea between Alaska and Russia.
Sponsors are people or companies that pay to support someone's trip.
A survival kit is a set of basic tools and supplies for staying alive outdoors.
Authorities are the people in charge, such as officials who give permission.
The Andes are a long chain of high mountains in South America.

background_read: Karl Bushby set out to walk all the way around the world, moving only on foot or by swimming.
Such a journey means crossing whole continents, high mountains and icy seas, with no car, plane or boat to help.
Travellers on very long walks usually carry their supplies and rely on strangers for food and shelter along the way.
His route took him across the Americas, over the Bering Strait into Asia and finally back across Europe to England.
